 CHIEF JUSTICE ROBERTS:  We'll hear
argument first this morning in Case 25-5930,
 Maxwell versus Dinis.
 Ms. Hansford.
 ORAL ARGUMENT OF MASHA G. HANSFORD
 ON BEHALF OF THE PETITIONER
 MS. HANSFORD: Mr. Chief Justice, and
may it please the Court:
 Mr. Maxwell's claim in this case is
that he's being held in prison in violation of
federal law because the First Step Act requires
his release from prison and transfer to home
confinement or to a halfway house. That is a
distinct and lower level of custody.
 That claim falls squarely within the
text of the federal habeas statute because it
asserts that Respondent, the Warden of
 Mr. Maxwell's prison, is holding him "in
custody in violation of the laws of the United
States." It also falls within the core
 historical province of the Great Writ.  And it
is materially indistinguishable from this
Court's decision in Preiser against Rodriguez,
